The biggest U.S. bank failure in more than two years just happened — quietly, on a Friday night.

Regulators shut United Fidelity Bank of Evansville, Indiana, on Nov. 27. It held about $5.9 billion in assets and $4.5 billion in deposits (as of Sept. 30). North Carolina's First Citizens Bank stepped in and took over the deposits, so every customer automatically became a First Citizens customer and kept their full balance — no one lost insured money.

The FDIC estimates the collapse will cost its Deposit Insurance Fund about $1.83 billion. That fund isn't taxpayer money — it's filled by fees every U.S. bank pays, and a hit this size is one the whole industry shares. It's the 7th U.S. bank failure of 2026, and the largest since April 2024.

My take: this is the system doing its job — insured depositors protected, a buyer lined up overnight. But seven failures in a year is worth watching. The quiet lesson: know whether your money sits under the $250,000 insured limit, per depositor, per bank.

Is all of your money actually FDIC-insured, or have you ever checked? 👇
